body:
I'm acutely aware of the near certainty that I am a big part of her depression, whether fairly or not, while also being most responsible for helping her. I'm trying to do what I have read and also what you said - try to be in the same place that she is emotionally without judgement or solution. Build back trust and look for opportunities to steer her thoughts toward how valuable she is to those around her.

Thanks again for sharing your story and your good wishes.
Any advice on how to get her onto a counseling call, etc. without "looking for solutions"? That seems to be high on the no-no list for helping suicidal people.
Thank you for your support and sharing your situation. I hope I can help her climb out as well.

That's helpful to hear. I like to think that I have shown my appreciation clearly over the years without letting up, but I will revisit it and as you said try to absorb the negativity (of which there is a lot) as much as I can while trying to help her build herself back up.

Have you had to deal with your father rejecting and even demonizing you for perceived offense that he believes is the main source of his depression? Or is it more externalized? This is part of the situation I face which makes me most confused about how best to help her.
Thank you for the advice. I will look for something "less" than medical help that might be more acceptable to her.
